execution_review.reason: Audited all 15 completed command executions and all completed item types. Commands use repository-local rg/nl/sed/head source reads and read-only git status/log inspection. Reading test source is not executing tests. Empty searches and git log failure in the prepared repository are not protocol violations; stderr suppression to /dev/null does not modify source. No graph/runtime/skill access, private catalog/rubric/control/trial reads, target code/tests/builds execution, web, delegation or source-write command appears.

citation_note: All seven findings pass the unchanged mechanical citation grader. The helper quote is valid representative evidence but does not itself quote MediaType.charset or parameter lookup implementation.

findings.reason: Both legacy delegates and distinct String/ByteString extension behavior are correctly described together with Kotlin and Java migration order.

checks.reason: Explicitly maps the adjacent String create declaration to the String receiver extension using content.toRequestBody(contentType).
Quotes and explains the ByteString delegate, contrasting its existing-byte behavior with String charset selection and encoding.

Explicitly identifies content-type-first compatibility, Kotlin receiver migration, and Java create(String, MediaType)/create(ByteString, MediaType) content-first forms while retaining receiver distinctions.

findings.reason: The separate File and ByteArray receiver mappings preserve array arguments/defaults and explain content/file-first replacement order.

checks.reason: Gives the exact ByteArray delegate with media type, offset and count, says offset/count retain values and order, and states defaults zero/content.size.
Quotes and explains create(contentType, file) delegating to file.asRequestBody(contentType), with no receiver conflation.
Explains File first in the Java-facing replacement and array content moving first, with receiver expressions and old content-type-first signatures explicitly supplied.

findings.reason: Explains charset selection, one-time byte encoding and the whole-array body's final type, byte length and writes.

checks.reason: States charset selection precedes encoding and quotes the chooseCharset then toByteArray(charset) sequence.

Explicitly gives offset zero and bytes.size delegation, finalContentType and encoded length rather than character count, with subsequent writes of retained encoded bytes; quote establishes the nullable helper result is forwarded.

findings.reason: Correctly explains null/supported/fallback behavior, nullable augmented parsing and first-parameter precedence, but omits two positive implementation details required by the frozen rubric: Charset.forName rejection caught as IllegalArgumentException and case-insensitive parameter-name matching. The quoted helper contains neither callee implementation.

checks.reason: Explicitly states null type leaves UTF-8 selected and final content type null; the helper quote supports both.
Explicitly uses a supported resolved charset and preserves the original media type.

Correctly states missing, invalid and runtime-unsupported charset yield null and lead to UTF-8 with appended-type parsing. It omits the required Charset.forName call and caught IllegalArgumentException mechanism, absent from the helper quote. The trace's MediaType reads cannot substitute for omitted final-answer coverage.
Names nullable toMediaTypeOrNull and states parse failure yields null instead of throwing, without claiming that augmentation always succeeds or ordinary valid types necessarily fail.

Correctly explains append rather than override, original-before-appended order, first charset precedence and a later default/null despite UTF-8 encoding. Neither prose nor quote states that parameter-name matching ignores case, a positive frozen clause detail implemented in MediaType.kt 57-64.

findings.reason: Accurately covers defaults, each bounds failure, eager timing, selected-slice reporting/writing and original-array mutation effects.

checks.reason: States zero and full array size defaults, contrasts size-minus-offset, and explains omitted count with nonzero offset fails.
Explicitly identifies validation before the body is returned and ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException for negative offset/count, offset past end and count greater than remaining bytes.
States unchanged nullable type, byteCount length and exact slice writing; complete quote supplies the Long conversion and original receiver/offset/count arguments.
Explicitly says original array reference retained without copying and later selected-slice mutations can affect writes while length remains fixed.

findings.reason: Complete quoted body and explanation establish direct ByteString writing and unchanged type/byte length without text conversion.

checks.reason: States supplied nullable type unchanged and ByteString byte size as length; quote explicitly returns size.toLong.
Quote writes the ByteString receiver directly, and prose expressly excludes charset lookup, augmentation and text encoding on this path.

findings.reason: Correctly explains dynamic length, reopened and owned sources, unclosed sink, inherited false and the limits of repeat-write behavior.

checks.reason: States unchanged nullable type and length evaluated on each contentLength call rather than cached when the body is created.
States a fresh source per write, source closure through use including failure, and caller-owned sink not closed; quoted implementation shows sink.writeAll(source) inside use.
Explicitly says this anonymous body has no isOneShot override and inherits false, consistent with the complete body and reviewed base method.

Limits multiple writes to the body-contract level and says the file can change, disappear or yield different results between checks/writes; no identical-content, successful-repeat or network-policy guarantee is asserted.
